{{recipesummary|category=Sauce recipes|servings=4|time=1 hour, 45 minutes|difficulty=2
}}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of The United States]] | [[Cookbook:Italian-American_cuisine|Italian-American Cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Sauces|Sauces]]

'''Bolognese sauce''', not to be confused with ''[[Wikipedia:Ragù alla bolognese|ragù alla bolognese]]'', is the tomato-based meat sauce that usually accompanies certain pasta, like [[Wikipedia:Spaghetti|spaghetti]] and [[Wikipedia:Rigatoni|rigatoni]], and used to top [[Wikipedia:Lasagne|lasagne]] in restaurants, in North America.

While pasta sauce served in homes usually includes vegetables that are, or are a part of, a union between the [[Wikipedia:Mirepoix (cuisine)|mirepoix]] and [[Wikipedia:Holy trinity (cuisine)|holy trinity]], and sometimes mushrooms; [[Wikipedia:Spaghetti_bolognese#Spaghetti_alla_Bolognese|''spaghetti bolognese'']] or ''spaghetti with meat sauce'' served as "traditional" and in restaurants does not.

This recipe could be seen as a commercial, North American take on the authentic Italian version that traditionally uses minced veal; here, egg whites are mixed with ground beef to lighten the color and mute the taste.  Institutionally, the sauce's composition is typically only ground tomatoes, ground pork, and water.

== Ingredients ==

* 1.5 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] (675 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) of lean ground [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]], at room temperature
* 2 large [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]] whites, at room temperature
* 1 can (28 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 800 g) of stewed San Marzano or Roma (''Italian'') [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]
* 1 can (6 oz / 170 g) [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato paste]]
* 6 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], peeled
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive oil|olive oil]]
* [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|Bay leaf]]
* [[Cookbook:Oregano|Oregano]]

== Procedure ==

# Put a thick-bottomed pot over a medium-low heat with the oil and garlic.
# As the pot warms up, mix the beef and egg whites into a homogeneous paste.
# [[Cookbook:Mixing#Stirring|Stir]] the garlic cloves in the warming oil until the fragrance can be noted.
# Add the meat to the pot, stirring to break clusters into fine pieces, and cook until most of the juices have evaporated.
# Add the tomato paste and stir before adding the stewed tomatoes.
# Cover the pot, leaving a vent, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] at a low heat for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
# Turn off the heat and retrieve the garlic cloves, to either discard or mash them before re-adding to the sauce.
# Season according to taste, taking in consideration the salt content of the tomato products.
# Cover completely and let rest for half an hour, during which time preparation for assembly and plating can be done.
